title: Multi-AZ VPC peering, interface endpoints and Route53 DNS forwarding for Private Control Plane
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private in customer VPCs require a resilient control-plane connectivity pattern that supports multi-AZ private endpoints, cross-account peering, and DNS forwarding without exposing control plane services to the internet. This PR implements Terraform modules and Helm hooks in the private-installer to provision: 1) dedicated subnets per AZ for control-plane interface endpoints, 2) AWS Interface VPC Endpoints (VPCE) for SSM/EC2/SecretsManager/KMS used by the control plane, 3) cross-account VPC peering with optional route table propagation and security-group restrictions, 4) automated Route53 inbound/outbound endpoints and conditional forwarding rules so control plane hostnames resolve across peered VPCs, and 5) tight security group templates and example least-privilege IAM policies. Changes are split into small commits and include an at-scale test harness used in our perf-canary cluster. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module added: modules/vpc-control-plane - [x] Example usage in docs/examples/customer-vpc.md - [x] Helm post-install hook to create kube-side DNS records - [x] Integration test: multi-az peering smoke - [x] Security review and IAM suggestions included Scope: This is additive; defaults maintain existing installer behavior unless the new module is enabled via installer variables. Migration/Rollback: Enabling is opt-in; disabling runs plan that removes created resources. See release_notes for operational guidance. Links: Linear ENG-4129 (control-plane private connectivity), SUP-789 (customer support ticket prompting cross-account peering), design doc: /docs/private/vpc-controlplane-design.md
release_notes: Added optional VPC control plane module enabling multi-AZ interface endpoints, cross-account VPC peering helpers, Route53 inbound/outbound endpoints and conditional forwarding templates. Defaults are opt-in; see docs/examples/customer-vpc.md for migration steps and rollback guidance.
commits_summary: Init terraform module for vpc-control-plane with variables and outputs
Add interface endpoint resources and security-group templates
Implement cross-account peering helper with route propagation options
Add Route53 inbound/outbound endpoint and conditional forwarding scripts
Helm hook: create cluster-local DNS records on install/upgrade
Docs: example usage, operational runbook, and k8s hook notes
review_comments: Marisol: Can we default to creating endpoints in the same AZ subnets as the control-plane load balancer? A: Module exposes az_subnet_ids so operators can map AZs; updated README to clarify.

Leo: Need to ensure we add tags so customer cost allocation can filter installer-created resources. A: Added tagging to all resources with terraform variable 'resource_tags' and default set to installer meta tags.

Dmitri: Security group rules should be explicit host/port rather than CIDR open. A: tightened SGs to allow only control-plane CIDR and peered VPC ranges; documented troubleshooting steps for SG-related failures.
ci_checks: integration: multi-az peering smoke: initial run flaky (timeouts) -> fixed route propagation waits -> pass
e2e: dns resolution across peering: pass
notes_for_ops: Operator notes: To enable, set installer.use_control_plane_module=true and provide control_plane_peering_config with peer_account_id and peer_vpc_id. The module will create route entries; if you manage routes centrally, set manage_routes=false. When tearing down, run 'terraform plan' to see dependent resources; Route53 inbound endpoints can take up to 30 minutes to become available, and peering teardown requires route cleanup first.
security_review_summary: Security review completed by infra-security team: recommended KMS key policy adjustments for cross-account SecretsManager access and explicit IAM conditions for SSM. Applied least-privilege templates; flagged one follow-up to rotate installer-managed KMS keys to customer-managed keys in a future PR.
user_impact: Low by default. When enabled, customers gain private control plane connectivity across peered VPCs and full DNS resolution. Temporary transient failures can occur while Route53 endpoints and routes propagate; documented retry/backoff guidance included.
notes: This PR was tested against our internal perf-canary cluster across three AZs and one cross-account test VPC. All infra changes are behind feature flags in the installer; rollout to GA requires a follow-up announcement and updated quickstart templates.
